root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking a live portion from fire and extends to seeking, receiving, or transmitting something drawn from a source, especially light, knowledge, or guidance.
root_idea.development: The concrete firebrand or flame-portion provides the basis for figurative uses involving the acquisition or imparting of knowledge and guidance. The same fiery image is also applied to rapid fertilization in قَبِيسٌ.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form VIII perfect citation form.
Displayed as the nominal citation form قَبَسٌ.

senses.definition: To seek or acquire a share of light or illumination; figuratively, to seek knowledge or guidance from a source.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the form appears in a construction of seeking light from others: نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ, “we may acquire from your light.”

senses.definition: A firebrand or live portion taken from a flame or larger fire.
senses.usage_conditions: The item may be a burning brand, live coal, or burning piece taken from a main fire; the Quranic contexts concern obtaining such a source of fire or light.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or obtain fire from a source.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with fire as the sought object and a person or source introduced by مِنْ; this is the literal branch underlying the figurative Quranic use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take fire from another person or from a larger fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source may be expressed with مِنْ, and the object may be fire or a firebrand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To acquire or learn knowledge from someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of taking something from a source; the knowledge may be expressed as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To catch a fever from another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative use describing a fever acquired from an external source rather than arising spontaneously.
This denotes requesting or seeking fire, rather than merely taking it once obtained.
A figurative use modeled on seeking fire from a source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To light or kindle a fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative action involving the production or ignition of fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give or bring someone a firebrand or fire; figuratively, to teach or impart knowledge or good, and also to give property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative transfer to a beneficiary; the transferred object may be fire, knowledge, good, or property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek fire for someone else.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The beneficiary is the person for whom the fire is sought, not necessarily the person from whom it is obtained.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion or benefit derived from another; figuratively, subsistence received from another or a light of truth made manifest to a seeker.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of a portion taken from another’s fire or source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single act of taking fire; by idiom, a very brief visit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The brief-visit meaning occurs in the comparison كَقَبْسَةِ العَجْلَانِ, “like the hasty person’s single act of taking fire.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who takes or seeks fire; figuratively, one who acquires or seeks knowledge. In the plural القَوَابِسُ, it can denote those who teach people what is good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial noun with both literal fire-seeking and figurative knowledge-related uses; the teaching sense is specifically plural in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or object associated with a firebrand, especially lighted firewood or hardened charcoal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited lexical description distinguishes hardened charcoal that holds together from حُمَمَةٌ, charcoal that does not.
A rare reported lexical use, distinct in vocalization from قَبَسٌ “firebrand.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of ṭunbūr, a stringed musical instrument.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately attested supplemental lexical item.

Figurative acquisition or learning of knowledge.

Imparting knowledge or good and giving property.

Firebrand-related place or hardened combustible material.

cautions: The Quranic Form VIII occurrence is the imperfect first-person plural نَقْتَبِسْ; the public headword is normalized to the perfect citation form اِقْتَبَسَ.
The supplemental قَبُوسٌ entry is retained as a separately attested lexical item and is not treated as an ordinary derivational form of the Quranic headwords.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: Lane entry 7715 contains elliptical references to related fire-taking implements described as “the last two”; their exact individual headword assignment is not secure, so only the shared firebrand/live-coal branch and the explicitly stated figurative uses are assigned.
